framework: Twelve-dimension weighted scoring frozen before scoring, applied identically to all nine canonical families. Commercial attractiveness (market/pricing/channel opportunity) is scored and reported independently from release readiness (legal, technical, manufacturability, support, sellability). No legal, safety, licensing or conformity blocker can be offset by a high commercial score.
scoringFormula: commercialScore = round(sum(weights[d] * scores[d]), 3); scores 1-5 where 5 is most favourable

weightRationale.problemSeverity: The portfolio exists to solve a real, frequent and expensive problem; severity is the first commercial filter.
weightRationale.demandEvidence: Observable demand and public problem signals must outweigh internal enthusiasm.
weightRationale.differentiationPotential: A family that cannot be distinguished from a market benchmark has weak pricing power.
weightRationale.revenueAndContribution: Per-unit revenue potential drives payback and channel interest.
weightRationale.recurringRevenuePotential: Recurring revenue is the only route to a durable EMBARCARTE business model, but it is not assumed profitable.
weightRationale.distributionFeasibility: EMBARCARTE has no established channel; direct and installer routes differ materially.
weightRationale.installationSimplicity: Installation complexity transfers risk and cost to the customer and the channel.
weightRationale.developmentAndIntegrationReadiness: Families that are already partially verified can reach validation faster.
weightRationale.ipLicensingExposure: Higher score means lower IP/licensing exposure; unresolved GPL, chart or data rights cap the score.
weightRationale.conformityAndSafetyExposure: Higher score means lower conformity and safety exposure; safety-critical hardware scores low.
weightRationale.supportAndWarrantyBurden: Higher score means a lower expected support and warranty burden.
weightRationale.timeToValidatedReadiness: How quickly customer validation can start without manufacturing or certification dependencies.

families.rationale: Highest-severity, best-evidenced owner problem in the research: fragmented navigation, recurring chart/weather cost and several established software alternatives at EUR 49-149/year. It is the only family that can be distributed directly today (no hardware), so its commercial case is strong. Readiness is blocked by chart/data rights and source-IP clearance, so validation is commercial and qualitative, not a launch.

Demand is excellent (PredictWind USD 29-499/year, Windy at EUR 19) and distribution is direct, but MAREA WEATHER is a thin layer over providers with no granted redistribution rights. It is strategically essential to NAV but cannot be sold standalone before a provider agreement.

Unattended-vessel monitoring has the clearest recurring-revenue logic and real competitor anchors (Siren Marine USD 299.99 plus USD 225/year, Yacht Sentinel, Orca guard mode). Recurring acceptance is unproven and the alert-delivery pipeline is unverified, so the next step is customer validation, not hardware commitment.

A real consolidation problem exists and gateways are a genuine category (Digital Yacht EUR 240-300, Victron Cerbo EUR 240.09, PredictWind DataHub USD 299). Differentiation depends on multi-device orchestration and installer-grade integration that are not verified; the category is price-anchored and hardware-led.

Per-vessel B2B SaaS is where the recurring revenue actually is, but competitors price at EUR 150-259 per vessel per month for operationally broader products, and the platform is not implemented. The small-vessel beachhead cannot fund the programme alone, so FLEET is the strategic expansion path rather than the first product.

Receive-only AIS is a commodity: Digital Yacht AIS100 at EUR 360 is established, and the MAREA hypothesis cannot undercut it while the GPL decoder decision is unresolved. The customer value of a further receive-only receiver is weak; AIS as a software integration is more defensible than AIS as hardware.

SENSE modules only acquire commercial meaning as enablers of WATCH/PROTECT, where Victron SmartShunt at EUR 90.21 already occupies the battery-monitoring slot. Standalone sensor hardware is a low-differentiation, install-heavy category; defer until a monitoring use case is validated.

Established autopilot systems already cost EUR 2,050-3,083 installed-class packs, and an official accident report shows how rudder-feedback loss disables both autopilot and follow-up steering. Safety criticality caps the commercial score and the safety gate is BLOCKED; PILOT must not be advanced in MC-10 beyond concept comprehension.

A proprietary display competes directly with Raymarine Element 7 HV at EUR 659.45 and Orca's EUR 1,997 system, requires capital-intensive hardware certification and offers no evidenced advantage over using the customer's own tablet. The portfolio should rent the display surface, not build it.
